entities.name: ledgerRead
entities.text: /-- Rev 6: the one ledger read, `diagnosis-context` (P:755). `prepare-diagnosis` (P:769) and `production-readiness` (P:801) decide from it, before any injury is known. Order error 3: `route!` reads the ledger a second time (P:923-925), and that read has no state here. A runtime that reads twice conforms only while the two reads agree. M6a is to make `route!` use the context's read. Rev 8 note: with one read, a stale context overwrites a ledger file that changed between the read and coordination's persist. That is the one-read design taken literally, and it is pinned by `route-decides-from-the-context-read-not-a-second-read` (futon2 `6dd147e6a`). Rev 12 anchor (futon2 `3fe0a2b6d`, futon3c `c16a86952`): `(P diagnosis-context {:durable-ledger :active-injuries})`. The map has no `:status`, so no status literal is the site. Since then `route!` takes `(:meta-diagnosis-context opts)` and reads the ledger itself only when it is given no context (`(P route! durable)`), so order error 3 no longer arises from `run-opportunity!`. -/

entities.name: noActiveInjury
entities.text: /-- Rev 12 anchor (futon2 `3fe0a2b6d`, futon3c `c16a86952`): no ledger file, `(P prepare-diagnosis {:status :not-required :reason :meta-self-heal/no-durable-injury-ledger})` (#3); an empty active set, `(P prepare-diagnosis {:status :not-required :reason :meta-self-heal/no-active-injury})` (#6). `route!` then returns nil (`(P route! (when (seq (:injuries active))))`). -/

entities.name: activeInjury
entities.text: /-- Rev 12 anchor (futon2 `3fe0a2b6d`, futon3c `c16a86952`): `(P prepare-diagnosis :else)`: the ledger loaded, the active set computed and is non-empty, and `produce-diagnosis!` is called on its first injury id. That branch has no status literal of its own. -/

entities.name: activeSetUnavailable
entities.text: /-- Rev 6, row #5: the ledger loaded, but `ledger/active-injuries` did not return `:computed` (P:780, `:diagnosis-active-set-unavailable`). A terminal refusal. Rev 12 anchor (futon2 `3fe0a2b6d`, futon3c `c16a86952`): the observation `(P prepare-diagnosis {:status :unavailable :reason :meta-self-heal/diagnosis-active-set-unavailable})`, then the refusal `(R run-opportunity! {:status :refused :reason :meta-self-heal/active-set-unavailable})` in the first `cond` arm. `(P route! :meta-self-heal/active-set-unavailable)` is the same guard for a caller that is not `run-opportunity!`; from `run-opportunity!` it is not reached, because the R arm ends the click on the same context first. -/

entities.name: retryClick
entities.text: /-- Rev 7: the start of a retry click. Its options carry `:meta-repair-retry` (S:989-995): the child of a parent that ended `:awaiting-retry`, launched only after the parent click is durably complete. It makes no ledger read of its own and no diagnosis (R:473-477). It carries the acceptance observation `:acceptance-retry-not-prepared` (#22), which is typed, not a state. Rev 12 anchor (futon2 `3fe0a2b6d`, futon3c `c16a86952`): `(S close-click! :meta-repair-retry)` sets the option, in the child `click!` it launches after the parent's release. In `run-opportunity!` the branch is `(R run-opportunity! retry)`, and its one site is the observation `(R run-opportunity! {:status :not-required :reason :meta-self-heal/acceptance-retry-not-prepared})`. -/

Rev 12 anchor (futon2 `3fe0a2b6d`, futon3c `c16a86952`): `(P attributable-retry-readiness {:status :ready :attribution})`, then `(R run-opportunity! retry)` runs `run-ordinary-opportunity!`. -/

Rev 12 anchor (futon2 `3fe0a2b6d`, futon3c `c16a86952`): before the reviewer is called: from `(P read-acceptance-proposal)`, `:meta-self-heal/acceptance-proposal-pin-unavailable`, `:meta-self-heal/acceptance-proposal-pin-mismatch`, `:meta-self-heal/acceptance-proposal-unreadable`, `:meta-self-heal/acceptance-proposal-not-proposed`, `:meta-self-heal/acceptance-proposal-review-state-invalid`, `:meta-self-heal/acceptance-proposal-identity-mismatch`, that function's `:meta-self-heal/acceptance-proposal-source-mismatch` and `:meta-self-heal/acceptance-proposal-not-concrete`; `(P admit-acceptance! :meta-self-heal/acceptance-run-port-unavailable)`, `(P admit-acceptance! :meta-self-heal/acceptance-review-port-unavailable)`, `(P admit-acceptance! :meta-self-heal/acceptance-run-refused)` (a run that threw lands here), `(P admit-acceptance! :meta-self-heal/acceptance-test-passes-before-repair)`. Rev 14 anchor (futon2 `43bb57fc7`; C, T and L unchanged since `d0a890f22`): `(C coordinate ledger/append-retry-result)`, the `:else` arm of the retry receipt. The status is computed, `(get-in reopened [:entry :state])` (C:426 at this HEAD), and is `:reopened` when `(L append-retry-result :reopened)` takes its second arm. -/

Rev 14 anchor (futon2 `43bb57fc7`; C, T and L unchanged since `d0a890f22`): `(C coordinate ledger/append-retry-result)`, the same computed status (C:426 at this HEAD), `:abandoned` when `(L append-retry-result :attempt-limit-exhausted)` takes its first arm. A second abandoned literal exists; it is `RetryNext.abandoned .retryBudgetSpent`, not this constructor: `(not C coordinate-queued-retry :retry-budget-spent)`. -/

The production retry port only persists and enqueues, so this is the closing status a production click is expected to reach. The M4a shape does not name it (finding). Rev 14 anchor (futon2 `43bb57fc7`; C, T and L unchanged since `d0a890f22`): `(C coordinate-queued-retry :awaiting-retry)` (C:248 at this HEAD), returned by `coordinate` through its `(= :queued (:status retry-receipt))` arm, when `ledger/pending-requeue` finds nothing. -/

entities.name: retryInconclusive
entities.text: /-- Rev 8: the retry click ran but did not test the repair (`RetryClickOutcome.closing`). The injury is neither discharged nor reopened, and the transaction stays `:enacted` and active. Rev 14 anchor (futon2 `43bb57fc7`; C, T and L unchanged since `d0a890f22`): not a `coordinate` status. It is the retry click's `(T integrate :retry-inconclusive)` observation: the non-injury arm for every reason except a successful task outcome (T:236), `(not T classify :successful-task-outcome)`, and `(T append-other-injury-retry-observation :retry-inconclusive)` (T:189). -/

Rev 13 anchor (futon2 `9d3026e1a`, T unchanged since `d0a890f22`): `(T classify :successful-task-outcome)`, the `non-injury-reason` arm for a nil failure kind and an outcome in `successful-outcomes`; `integrate` then appends `(T integrate :discharged)` for the enacted entry. -/

entities.name: sameInjury
entities.text: /-- `:injury` with the enacted entry's injury id: `append-retry-result` (T:244, L:299-317). The retry failed for the same cause. Rev 13 anchor (futon2 `9d3026e1a`, T unchanged since `d0a890f22`): `(T integrate ledger/append-retry-result)`, the arm `(= :enacted (:state previous))` with `(= (:retry-click previous) (:click-id classification))`; the transition is the computed `(get-in appended [:entry :state])`, so there is no keyword literal. -/

entities.name: otherInjury
entities.text: /-- `:injury` with a different injury id, and the record is ingested. Cited at futon2 `b5dd9269c` (M10b-4). `integrate` binds `other-injury-retry?` (T:247-251). If the different id is unknown, it opens a new injury (T:253-266). If it is active, it appends a `:repeated-active-injury` observation (T:288-297). Either way it then appends the attributed `:retry-inconclusive` observation for the enacted entry through `append-other-injury-retry-observation` (T:185-196). The enacted entry's state is untouched. Added in rev 8 (finding) and widened by the rev 8 review. Rev 11 split off the refused arms as `otherInjuryRefused`. Rev 13 anchor (futon2 `9d3026e1a`, T unchanged since `d0a890f22`), re-anchored in rev 16 to the call the function makes: `(T append-other-injury-retry-observation ledger/append-observation)` which appends the retry-inconclusive observation for the enacted entry. The function is called from `(T integrate)` on the `(nil? previous)` arm with transition `:open` and on the `ledger/active-states` arm with transition `:active-injury-retained`. -/

entities.name: otherInjuryRefused
entities.text: /-- Rev 11: `:injury` with a different injury id, and the record is refused, not ingested (at `b5dd9269c`). This happens when the different id is itself `:enacted` and this click is not its retry click (`:injury/retry-click-mismatch`, T:268-286), or when the different id is terminal (`:injury/terminal-history-requires-new-transaction`, T:299-300). `integrate` returns `{:status :refused}` with no ledger, so no observation is written and the pin stays un-ingested. It is a separate constructor, not an unobserved `otherInjury`, because the coordinator receives a refusal rather than an ingested record without an observation. Under the law it is still inconclusive for the enacted injury. Rev 13 anchor (futon2 `9d3026e1a`, T unchanged since `d0a890f22`): `(T integrate :injury/retry-click-mismatch)`, `(T integrate :injury/terminal-history-requires-new-transaction)`. -/

entities.name: ordinarySelectionAbstention
entities.text: /-- `:ordinary-selection-abstention` (T:82): an abstention. Rev 13 anchor (futon2 `9d3026e1a`, T unchanged since `d0a890f22`): `(T abstention-reason :ordinary-selection-abstention)`, the `:else` arm, reached from `classify` when the failure kind is `:abstained` and the route is configured. The `{:abstained :ordinary-selection-abstention}` entry of `explicit-non-injury-kinds` is never read for it: `classify` takes the `:abstained` branch first. -/

entities.name: recordUnreadable
entities.text: /-- Rev 9: the retry click left no record that can be read. Then nothing reaches `integrate`, and the entry stays `:enacted`. Absence is evidence of neither success nor failure, so this is inconclusive (the 2026-09-24 rule that absence must not read as a value). Rev 13 anchor (futon2 `9d3026e1a`, T unchanged since `d0a890f22`): no producing site in T for a retry that wrote no record: nothing is ingested. A record that exists but cannot be ingested stops before `integrate` at `(meta-injury-store ingest-record-file! :store/record-ingest-failed)` or at `read-one-form`'s non-`:read` result (that file has no tag), and a record that does not classify stops at `(T classify :terminal-record/malformed)`. Reading those as this constructor is my reading, not something the Lean states. -/

entities.name: retryBudgetSpent
entities.text: /-- Rev 9 (new, M10b): the re-queue budget for inconclusive retries is spent. A re-queue authors nothing, so it does not count against `:attempt-limit`. Rev 15 anchor (futon2 `5a066d9ab`; C and L unchanged since `aa3ec313b`): `(L append-requeue :retry-budget-spent)` (L:397), the arm where the entry's requeue count has reached the ledger's retry limit (L:394), with the attempt carried over unchanged. `(C coordinate-queued-retry :retry-budget-spent)` (C:261) returns it, after reading the appended entry's state (C:260), before any retry port call. `validate-ledger` accepts it only when the requeue count equals the retry limit (L:174-176). -/

entities.name: queued
entities.text: /-- A fresh retry click is queued for the same enacted entry. Rev 15 anchor (futon2 `5a066d9ab`; C and L unchanged since `aa3ec313b`): `(C coordinate-queued-retry ledger/append-requeue)` (C:258), on the arm where `ledger/pending-requeue` (C:247, L:331) finds the attributed observation, and then `(L append-requeue :enacted)` (L:402), a new enacted entry with a new retry click. The entry's fields: `attempt` is the ledger's attempt, copied from the previous entry (L:392); `requeues` is the ledger's requeue count, read at L:390 and written incremented at L:404. On the `recur` (C:267), C reads that count back (C:232) and, being positive, calls the retry port with the requeue ordinal (C:233-238). The queued click then ends the same way as `awaitingNothingQueued`: the new entry has no observation yet, so `coordinate` returns the awaiting-retry status. In the code the two constructors differ by the appended entry and the port call, not by the status. -/
